assumptions: 'tool-call turn' = a row whose tool_calls list is non-empty. In the three tool files every follow-up row also carries tool_calls, so the row-level exposed set is exactly the tool_calls set (186 rows).

The card's run-level rule ('kind == tool-followup present in the same run') is applied on run_id; each of the three tool files holds exactly one run, so the run-level set is the whole file (212 rows).

Era is a property of the writer and the writer is inferred from two axes (seam-field presence; rows-file mtime vs the WIRE-CLIENT landing 2026-10-26T14:53:28Z). Both axes select the same single file. No log line names a commit, so the classification is as strong as those two axes and no stronger.

The 3 legacy files (232 rows) are labelled undatable AS TTFT SOURCES because they carry no TTFT column at all; they were written before the seam (written_before_seam true) and contribute 0 rows to every published latency figure, so their era is moot rather than unknown.
wall clock for a row without wall_ms is round(latency_s*1000, 3) — the expression client.collect_stream() uses to fill wall_ms; validated on the 6 rows carrying both columns (6 of 6 match).
